decision_records.defer_or_adopt_reason: Create adapter IO contracts and node lifecycle skeletons first; do not install or adopt LangGraph until a later owner-approved runtime PR.
decision_records.evidence_excerpt_summary: The official overview frames LangGraph as a low-level orchestration framework and runtime for long-running stateful agents, with durable execution, streaming, human-in-the-loop, persistence, and memory capabilities. It also says LangGraph can be used without LangChain.
decision_records.fit_for_avf: Use as the first evaluated stateful agent graph adapter because AVF already has Orchestrator, Router, Safety, Codex Planner, and Evidence Writer roles.
decision_records.primary_source_claim: AVF runtime adapter should evaluate a stateful graph model for long-running agent orchestration.
risk_notes: Keep agent nodes deterministic until external model and tool calls are separately approved.
Require human gates before any live action node can run.

decision_records.defer_or_adopt_reason: Temporal is too heavy for the current repo-local compiler; first define workflow state, retry, timeout, and evidence event contracts.
decision_records.evidence_excerpt_summary: The Temporal docs describe Temporal as an open-source platform for reliable applications and emphasize crash-proof execution that resumes where work left off after crashes, network failures, or infrastructure outages.
decision_records.fit_for_avf: Use later for crash-resumable, long-running venture runs after the local kernel has stable run states and idempotency rules.
decision_records.primary_source_claim: AVF durable workflow phases should evaluate crash-resumable workflow execution.
risk_notes: Do not introduce worker services or deployment assumptions in the foundation branch.
Require explicit rollback and resume semantics before adoption.

decision_records.defer_or_adopt_reason: Define telemetry event names and claim-boundary fields now; delay SDK or collector adoption until runtime exists.
decision_records.evidence_excerpt_summary: The OpenTelemetry docs define it as an observability framework and toolkit for generation, export, and collection of telemetry such as traces, metrics, and logs, and describe it as open source, vendor-neutral, and tool-agnostic.
decision_records.fit_for_avf: Use as the future trace, metric, and log vocabulary for AVF runs, cells, validators, costs, and evidence events.
decision_records.primary_source_claim: AVF observability should use a standard traces, metrics, and logs model.
risk_notes: Avoid logging prompts, credentials, or sensitive payloads verbatim.
Keep repo-local validation independent from collector availability.

decision_records.defer_or_adopt_reason: Draft tool registry and approval contracts first; do not run MCP servers or external tools in this planning pass.
decision_records.evidence_excerpt_summary: The MCP docs define MCP as an open-source standard for connecting AI applications to external systems, including data sources, tools, and workflows. The same page positions MCP as a standardized connector boundary for AI applications.
decision_records.fit_for_avf: Use as the future tool/plugin boundary so AVF can connect tools through explicit capability, permission, and evidence contracts.
decision_records.primary_source_claim: AVF tool integration should use an explicit tool protocol boundary before plugin execution.
decision_records.primary_source_title: What is the Model Context Protocol?
risk_notes: Treat tool descriptions and tool outputs as untrusted inputs.
Block write, publish, deploy, scraping, and account automation tools until owner approval and policy gates exist.

decision_records.defer_or_adopt_reason: Do not add a live provider gateway before model policy, credential handling, and offline validation gates are defined.
decision_records.evidence_excerpt_summary: The LiteLLM repository describes LiteLLM as an open-source AI Gateway for 100+ LLM providers using the OpenAI format. The official docs also describe a self-hosted OpenAI-compatible proxy and gateway surface for models, agents, and MCP.
decision_records.fit_for_avf: Use later as the provider-independent model gateway candidate after AVF has model routing, cost, policy, and redaction contracts.
decision_records.primary_source_claim: AVF model plane should evaluate a provider-independent LLM gateway.
risk_notes: Provider keys, base URLs, and model choices require explicit owner configuration.
Gateway traces must preserve claim boundaries and avoid public-readiness claims.

decision_records.defer_or_adopt_reason: Serving infrastructure is outside the current Web-first repo-local control plane; keep it as an approved future integration candidate only.
decision_records.evidence_excerpt_summary: The vLLM repository describes vLLM as a fast, easy-to-use library for LLM inference and serving, with throughput and memory management features. The docs note an OpenAI-compatible API server and broad model/hardware support.
decision_records.fit_for_avf: Use later as an open-model serving candidate when local or self-hosted inference becomes a real bottleneck.
decision_records.primary_source_claim: AVF model plane should evaluate open model serving for later approved runtime phases.
risk_notes: Do not assume GPU capacity, model weights, or serving readiness.
Require license, model-card, resource, and safety review before any serving work.

decision_records.defer_or_adopt_reason: This is not a runtime dependency for AVF; it informs future web-agent evaluation and safety limits.
decision_records.evidence_excerpt_summary: The arXiv record describes WebArena as a realistic and reproducible web-agent environment with long-horizon benchmark tasks. It reports that the best GPT-4-based baseline agent achieved 14.41% end-to-end success versus 78.24% human performance, supporting approval-gated web automation rather than broad unsupervised action.
decision_records.fit_for_avf: Use as evidence that web autonomy must remain sandboxed, approval-gated, and benchmarked rather than broad unsupervised web action.
decision_records.primary_source_claim: AVF web automation should remain approval-gated because autonomous web agents need evidence-backed limits.
decision_records.primary_source_title: WebArena: A Realistic Web Environment for Building Autonomous Agents
risk_notes: Do not implement live browsing, scraping, posting, or account automation from this source record.
Use benchmark evidence to define stop conditions and human approval gates.

selection_rules: Prefer contract skeletons before runtime adoption.
Use primary-source claims as planning evidence, not as dependency approval.
Keep dependency adoption, runtime integration, provider calls, and external actions behind later owner gates.
Treat web autonomy as sandboxed and approval-gated until benchmarked.
